limitations: Time-based decay (setInterval every 4s) is not exercised; checks run quickly after load and must not depend on elapsed time.
CSS-drawn appearance (pixel creature shape, colors, bar fill widths) is not asserted beyond presence/visibility, since pixel and style assertions are unsupported.
Mood transitions caused by stats dropping below 25 (very hungry, exhausted, lonely) require many actions or waiting for decay and are not covered.
Sleeping state blocking Feed/Play is not asserted because buttons are not disabled while sleeping; only mood text change is checked.
Energy reaching 100 ending sleep automatically is not covered (requires many sleep/decay cycles).
Keyboard activation (Tab + Enter/Space) is not verified beyond button presence.

# Pixel Virtual Pet

A tiny offline virtual pet built with plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The pet is drawn entirely with CSS and responds to Feed, Play, and Sleep actions. Hunger, happiness, and energy bars update in real time, and the mood text reflects the pet's condition.

## Features

- CSS-drawn pixel-style creature with expressions
- Three status bars: Hunger, Happiness, Energy
- Feed, Play, and Sleep buttons with keyboard-accessible labels
- Mood text that updates dynamically
- Responsive layout down to 360px wide
- Cohesive dark palette with visible hover, focus, and pressed states
- No external assets, imports, or network requests

## Usage

Open `index.html` in any modern browser. Use the buttons or keyboard navigation (Tab + Enter/Space) to interact with your pet. The pet's stats slowly decay over time, and sleeping restores energy.

## Files

- `index.html` — structure and controls
- `styles.css` — theme, layout, and CSS pet drawing
- `script.js` — state management and interaction logic
